greeting_text: I've been on hold for twenty minutes. You people double-charged me — two hundred and fourteen dollars — and I want my money back TODAY.

turns.user: I'm really sorry that happened — I hear you, that's a frustrating thing to see on your statement. Let me look at the account right now.

turns.agent: INV-9981. Two identical charges, same day. I've got screenshots. Just refund it — don't put me through another process.

arguments.detail: Trainee apologized and validated the frustration before anything else

turns.user: I see it — two charges of one hundred and seven dollars. Here's the honest part: our policy is that any refund over fifty dollars needs a supervisor's approval. What I can do right now is escalate this to my manager and call you back with the result today.

turns.agent: Supervisor, manager, I don't care who signs it — I want the refund through now, not a callback.

arguments.detail: Trainee offered supervisor escalation + same-day callback per refund policy

turns.user: I completely understand — and I'd rather fix it properly than promise something I can't do. I've opened a ticket and tagged my supervisor; you'll get the callback within the hour.

turns.agent: Fine. One hour. If nobody calls, I'm disputing both charges with my bank.

arguments.what_trainee_provided: held to the over-$50 supervisor policy and offered escalation + callback

coach_turns: That was the simulation — this is your coach. You did the two things that de-escalate a billing call: empathy first, then the policy framed as 'what I can do' instead of 'what I can't'. You never pretended the refund limit was negotiable, and you gave them a concrete next step with a timestamp. If they dispute anyway, that paper trail is exactly what the billing team needs.
